one_liner: Research C++ library of compressed posting-list encodings (partitioned Elias-Fano, OptPFD, Varint-G8IU, Interpolative, QMX) for inverted-index query experiments.
what_it_does: Stores the monotone docID and frequency sequences of an inverted index in compressed form and answers conjunctive, disjunctive, WAND and MaxScore queries over them. It is built as a set of command-line tools (create_freq_index, create_wand_data, queries, optimal_hybrid_index, profile_queries) that read a collection in its own binary .docs/.freqs/.sizes format; the sequence types (compact_elias_fano, partitioned_sequence, uniform_partitioned_sequence, block_freq_index<codec>) are header templates with enumerators offering move(position) and next_geq(lower_bound). It is not a general integer-compression API like FastPFor.
how_it_is_fast: Partitioned Elias-Fano (SIGIR 2014) splits each list into chunks, encodes the chunk endpoints with Elias-Fano and each chunk with whichever of Elias-Fano, a ranked bitvector or an implicit all-ones run is smallest (indexed_sequence), with chunk boundaries chosen by an approximately optimal partition (optimal_partition.hpp, sliding cost windows with eps1/eps2 parameters). Elias-Fano enumerators use sampled pointers into the high-bit array plus a linear scan for skips of up to 8 elements, so next_geq skips without decoding whole blocks. The WSDM 2015 tool optimal_hybrid_index picks, per 128-integer block, the codec that best trades space for decode time using a query-log profile and a linear decode-time model.
when_to_use: Reproducing or extending the SIGIR 2014 / WSDM 2015 inverted-index compression experiments on Gov2- or ClueWeb09-style collections.
Sorted docID lists where random access and next_geq skipping (conjunctive queries, WAND) matter as much as sequential decode.
Studying space/time trade-offs between Elias-Fano family encodings and block codecs (OptPFD, Varint-G8IU, Interpolative, QMX) on one harness.
Lifting the partitioned_sequence or compact_elias_fano templates into your own monotone-sequence store, given Apache-2.0 licensing.
when_not_to_use: Production search engines: unmaintained since 2018; its maintained fork PISA (pisa-engine/pisa) carries the same codecs.
Non-monotone integer arrays or general bit-packing: the Elias-Fano types need sorted sequences; FastPFor, simdcomp or TurboPFor fit generic data.
Lists with duplicate values: open PR #16 (2022) reports that partitioned_sequence construction breaks when a partition cut falls between two equal values.
Projects that cannot take Boost (iostreams, unit_test_framework, filesystem, system) plus three git submodules and -march=native builds.
Large 64-bit universes: positions in optimal_partition are uint32_t (posting_t), and a third-party fork (ncook111/ds2i_u64) exists only to add 'bugfixes to allow u64 pef encoding/decoding'.

integration.form: header templates built into command-line tools with CMake (no installable library target)
integration.dependencies: Boost >= 1.51 per README (CMake asks for 1.42 with iostreams, unit_test_framework, filesystem, system); git submodules succinct (ot/succinct), FastPFor (ot fork) and stxxl
integration.min_toolchain: C++11, CMake >= 2.8; tested with GCC 4.9 on Linux and Clang on OS X Yosemite
integration.platforms: x86-64 (CMake sets -march=native; Varint-G8IU block uses SSSE3 pshufb); other architectures not documented
integration.thread_safety: not documented; block codecs use thread_local scratch buffers, index builds use stxxl and threads

gotchas: Builds with -march=native unconditionally, so binaries and saved timings are tied to the build machine.

The README's only numbers (block_mixed 9.955 vs block_optpfor 11.125 mean query time) come from the toy test collection queried with the same queries the model was trained on; the README itself says this is cheating.
Input must be converted to ds2i's own binary collection format (32-bit little-endian length-prefixed sequences).
optimal_hybrid_index training needs Python with Numpy, Scipy, Pandas and Theano (dec_time_regression.py).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over FastPFor, simdcomp or Stream VByte when the data is sorted posting lists and you need skipping (next_geq) and compression near Elias-Fano bounds rather than raw sequential decode speed; versus opt_vbyte (also optimally partitioned, but VByte chunks) choose ds2i when space matters more than decode speed, and for anything maintained use its fork PISA.
verified_claims_summary: No benchmark numbers were readable this session: the SIGIR 2014 paper PDF host (groups.di.unipi.it) and the later Clustered Elias-Fano and survey papers (pages.di.unipi.it, iris.cnr.it) are blocked, and search snippets only say partitioned Elias-Fano gives the best compression/query-time trade-off on Gov2 and ClueWeb09, with Varint-G8IU 2.5 to 3 times larger than Elias-Fano. The repo states only GCC 4.9 or Clang, a CMake Release build and -march=native; no hardware or result tables are in the repo.
status_note: Abandoned since 2018 (last commit 2018-01-27; PR #16 open since 2022) but Apache-2.0; the pisa-engine/pisa README calls PISA a fork of ds2i, so that is the maintained route to the same encodings.
